definition-weighted-squared-expectation: SI Section III, p.S8, Eq. S.61: the weighted squared expectation is defined by the authors

theory_low.quark-theorem-1-statement: Theorem 1, Section 4.2: the proof (Appendix A.3.1) is an informal argument that takes the expected accuracy of a random model as that of a random guess. The bound formulas are lost in the text layer, so the conditions cannot be checked from the quotes.
theory_low.quark-theorem-1-proof-assumption: Appendix A.3.1: the key step (9) to (10) is an expectation about random models taken as a random guess, an assumption, not a proved result
theory_low.quark-size-independence-claim: Section 4.2 and footnote 3: a consequence of the Theorem 1 bound, whose proof is informal
theory_low.quark-vs-vqc-worst-case-argument: Section 4.2: an analytical argument against a worst case of the baseline, with the comparison step stated and not proved
theory_low.quark-theorem-2-statement: Theorem 2, Section 4.3: the proof (A.3.2) uses a near-uniform distribution assumption and an approximation step; the bound is lost in the text layer
theory_low.quark-kpd-tradeoff: Section 4.3: a trade-off argument whose bounds are lost in the text layer and which depends on alpha, beta and C
theory_low.quark-theorem-3-statement: Theorem 3, Section 4.3: the derivation (A.3.3) is approximate and the closed form and condition are lost in the text layer
theory_low.quark-theorem-3-derivation-approximation: Appendix A.3.3: the authors replace an exact ratio by a simpler power, an approximation
theory_low.quark-query-complexity: The value is accurate and the more careful of the two: it carries the authors' own softening ('some evidences'). The proofs are short informal derivations with approximation steps (Appendix A.3), so 'prove' is the authors' claim.
theory_low.zhang-u1-decoupling: Eq. 2 and Supplement p.7: a derivation in the R to infinity limit, not stated as a theorem with conditions
theory_low.zhang-spin-eb-reshaping: Supplement Eqs. 17-20: a construction with an example; the Heisenberg-limit step is taken from cited RPE work
theory_low.zhang-omega-rfe: Learning pure spin and boson coefficients (ii.): the Heisenberg-limit step is taken from cited RFE work
theory_low.zhang-eq6-displacement: Eq. 6 and Supplement pp.12-13: a standard displaced-oscillator formula with the derivation referred to [22]; the equation is not in the quotes
theory_low.zhang-trotter-scheme: Eq. 7, pp.3-4: stated for the idealized R to infinity limit; finite-R behavior is supported only by numerics and the Heisenberg-limit step uses cited RFE
theory_low.zhang-trotter-rfe-measurements: p.4: the polylog measurement scaling rests on cited RFE results and on the supplement's applicability argument, which is approximate
theory_low.zhang-dqs-scheme: Eqs. 8-9, p.4: the error formula is taken from cited distributed quantum sensing work
theory_low.zhang-scheme-tradeoff: p.4 and Discussion: the measurement-count comparison is the same claim graded low in zhang-trotter-rfe-measurements (it rests on cited RFE). Only the extra-gate cost of the Trotter scheme is a limit the authors state about their own method, and the value joins the two.
theory_low.zhang-omega-error-propagation-trotter: Supplement pp.8-9: a first-order Taylor argument without explicit constants
theory_low.zhang-omega-error-propagation-dqs: Supplement Eq. 24: the result assumes the frequency error already scales as O(1/T)
theory_low.zhang-rfe-applicability: Supplement p.10: an approximate argument that relies on a normal approximation and a large-sample assumption
theory_low.zhang-trace-distance-bound: Supplement Eq. 35: argued by reference to the method of cited work [19], approximating the bosonic state as a coherent state; the full proof is not given
theory_low.zhang-heisenberg-theorem: The value is the more exact statement of Theorem 1 (conditions 1 to 3 in the quotes). The theorem is not proved as one result: its parts rest on cited RFE and RPE results, on the R to infinity limit, and on numerics. The supplement states the trace-distance proof fails for the Trotter spin-boson coupling scheme.
theory_low.anyon-kernel-phase-symmetry: Appendix B, p.15: K_phi = K_-phi is stated as an implication of the permutation-level description with no derivation or proof in the paper
theory_low.anyon-kernel-identical-particle-subspace: Section III, p.6: a background statement about symmetric and antisymmetric subspace sizes, which is standard field knowledge (cited [44]). It is not derived or settled by this paper. The claim that the feature map relaxes the constraint is the authors' interpretation.
theory_low.noise-order-purity-approximation: Section II.3 Eq. (5), Appendix A.4: the Bessel form comes from a Poisson approximation and a Gaussian approximation (A35-A37), an approximation, not a proved result
theory_low.complexity-proportional-purity-derivatio: Section II.3, Eq. (6): derived under an assumed uniform overlap model (A29) and local linearization; the paper itself says idealized assumptions and relies on numerical validation
theory_low.generalization-gap-formula: Section II.3 Eq. (7), Appendix A.3 Eq. (A28): applies a cited local linear smoother result [47] under homoscedastic noise and a local approximation; cited and approximate
theory_low.surrogate-complexity-below-physical: Appendix B.1, Eq. (B3): the matrix inequality is shown, but the step to 'surrogate complexity is no greater' is stated without being worked out. The value also reports fitted effective counts, which are measured results.
theory_low.optimum-location-formula: Section II.8 Eq. (9), Appendix A.5 Eqs. (A46)-(A48): derived from the surrogate model under a local-regression and weak-overlap approximation; not a proved result
theory_low.optimum-shifts-low-noise-with-data: Section II.8: a consequence of the approximate surrogate-model formula (A46), not an independent result
theory_low.scaling-sqrt-g-complexity: Appendix A.4, Eq. (A38): an asymptotic argument under the surrogate model with the extra assumption q = g and a Gaussian approximation
theory_low.mse-bias-variance-competition: Appendix A.5, Eqs. (A43)-(A45): derived under the weak-overlap local approximation H = sP_T and homoscedastic noise; approximate
theory_low.noise-model-beyond-bernoulli: Appendix A.6: a sketched extension, not worked out or tested
theory_low.dp-evaluation-cost: Appendix B.3: an operation count for the authors' algorithm (O(n q g^2 d^3)) stated without a formal proof and with no timing
theory_low.thm1-naive-decoding-lambda4: Theorem 1 claims Theta(lambda^4), but the printed proof (SI Section II, Eq. S.59) ends in an upper bound O(lambda^4 ...). The lower-bound half is not derived, so it is not a proved result.
theory_low.thm1-formal-statement: Formal Theorem 1 claims a Theta bound, but the proof (S.42-S.59) ends with O(lambda^4 max(M0,M1)). It also uses an unproved step that the majority of local terms fail to commute with a number of stabilizers proportional to r. Not a proved result as stated.
theory_low.thm1-proof-ends-in-upper-bound: The quotes describe a proof that sets out to find a lower bound over all rotations alpha but ends with an O (upper) bound at S.59, using a majority-of-terms assumption. This is a gap in the proof, not a settled result.
theory_low.thm3-formal-statement: Theorem 3 formal (SI p.S11): the proof (Eqs. S.92-S.104) assumes e_alpha > 0 for small lambda, uses the inverse of the error Gram matrix epsilon, and assumes D independent errors. None of this appears in the statement or the quotes, which carry no such condition. Conditions are dropped, so not graded as a proved result.
theory_low.thm3-proof-construction-and-assumption: The quotes show the proof adds an assumption (e_alpha > 0 for small lambda) that is not in the theorem statement, and builds the unitary by Gram-Schmidt on near-orthonormal states. A construction with an added assumption, not a result of its own.
theory_low.qnn-decoder-quadratic-improvement: The value is accurate to the passages (Abstract, Theorem 3, p.5 on the 5-qubit case). It is the authors' comparison of an upper bound for QNN against the Theorem 2 scaling. It relies on Theorem 3, whose proof adds an unstated assumption, and the paper itself says the 5-qubit case shows no improvement in scaling. An author claim, not settled by the paper.

requote.anyon-kernel-scope-two-particle: regraded LOW at the team lead's decision: Section VI, pp.12-13: the claim that the two-particle regime is accessible with existing technology rests on cited experiments (Refs. 29, 39), not on this paper. 'Will require multipartite entangled inputs' is the authors' forecast. This is a feasibility claim and a field statement, not a limitation the paper states about its own results. Lowering is a certainty change for the team lead.
